p:cNvPr.descr: At the top left is 5-methylcytidine. It is a 6-sided ring structure. Its apical C bonds up to NH2, down and right to C, which bonds up and right to CH3 and double bonds down to C. C double bonds down to N, which bonds down to ribose (boxed) and up and left to C, which double bonds down to O and up to N, which double bonds up and right to the initial C. To the right is N6-methyladenosine. It consists of a 5-carbon ring and a 6-carbon ring. The top C of the 6-sided ring bonds up to NH, which bonds up to CH3. C bonds down and right to C, which double bonds down to C, which bonds down and left to N. N double bonds up and left to C, which bonds up to N, which double bonds up and right to C. To the right is the 5-carbon ring. Its apical N bonds down and right to C, which bonds down to N. N bonds down to ribose (boxed) and left to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds right to the initial C. Below is 5-methylguanosine. It is a 6-sided and 5-sided combination structure. On the left, the apical C of the 6-sided ring double bonds up to O, down and left to NH, which bonds down to C. C bonds down and left to NH, which bonds left to CH3. C double bonds right to N, which bonds up and right to C. C double bonds up to C, which bonds up and left to the initial C. To the right, the apical N of the 5-sided ring double bonds down and right to C, which bonds down to N. N bonds down to ribose (boxed), left to C, which double bonds up to C, which bonds up and right to N. To the right of this is 5-hydroxymethylcytidine. Its apical C bonds up to NH2, down and right to C, which bonds up and right to CH2OH and double bonds down to C. C double bonds down to N, which bonds down to ribose (boxed) and up and left to C, which double bonds down to O and up to N, which double bonds up and right to the initial C.
